analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10=0.6225, improving by 0.0113 over the reported 0.6112 baseline, within the hypothesized 0.005–0.015 gain. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.690, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.635, Electronics 0.435, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.730. Electronics improved from the reported 0.400; prior scores for the other categories were not supplied, so their regressions cannot be assessed. Results support minibatch supervised-edge masking as a useful change in this configuration, but do not establish the proposed training–inference mismatch as the cause. Allocated GPU time was 1431.36 seconds; no test results were used.
code_summary: One independently trained network and one selected checkpoint per category, with dataset routing and no ensemble. Each network uses 64-dimensional embeddings, three-layer LightGCN propagation, jointly trained recency-aware history attention, a vector gate initialized with bias 2.0, and learned item biases. Training retains sampled-softmax loss, 64 negatives excluding observed training items, embedding regularization, and Adam. Each minibatch removes all distinct supervised user–positive edges in both directions and recomputes symmetric degree normalization before propagation; supplied histories remain unchanged. Validation and prediction use the complete training graph. Nonpersistent topology metadata and cleared embedding caches prevent minibatch masks from entering inference. Diagnostics check duplicate removal, bidirectional masking, normalization, isolated-node finiteness, persistent adjacency integrity, gradients, and serialization parity. The predictor reconstructs the same architecture and strictly loads one checkpoint per category.
